record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Assume a signed graph Σ is unbalanced and has a Hamiltonian circle. Determine whether Σ must contain a negative Hamiltonian circle, a positive Hamiltonian circle, or both.

evidence.quote: S1. Assume Σ has a Hamiltonian circle and is unbalanced. Is there a negative Hamiltonian circle? A positive one? Ans. Unknown.

artifact.status_search_result: The general question remains open, but partial progress has been made for specific classes. In particular, recent work has characterized the existence of positive and negative Hamiltonian circles in signed complete graphs (a signed complete graph contains both a positive and a negative Hamiltonian circle iff it contains both a positive and a negative triangle), and related results have appeared for simple plane signed graphs and multisigned complete graphs. A noted exception class is unbalanced "necklaces" of balanced blocks, which have only negative Hamiltonian circles. The full general problem for arbitrary unbalanced signed graphs with a Hamiltonian circle does not appear to be fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian Cycles in Signed and Multisigned Complete Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A signed complete graph on n vertices contains both a positive and a negative Hamiltonian circle if and only if it also contains both a positive and a negative triangle.
status_evidence.claim: Partial resolution for signed complete graphs.
